items.headline: Physicists just saw quarks make waves in the Big Bang’s primordial soup
items.teaser: Physicists at CERN’s Large Hadron Collider have captured the clearest evidence yet that quark-gluon plasma, the scorching-hot matter that…
items.story:
Physicists at CERN’s Large Hadron Collider have captured the clearest evidence yet that quark-gluon plasma, the scorching-hot matter that filled the newborn universe, behaves like a true liquid. By tracking individual quarks as they blasted through the plasma, researchers saw them leave behind ripples, splashes, and swirling wakes much like a duck moving through water. The finding suggests this primordial “soup” is so dense that it can slow speeding quarks and respond collectively as a fluid.

items.story: ചാവക്കാട് കുടുംബരോഗ്യ കേന്ദ്രത്തിലെ ജൂനിയര്‍ ഹെല്‍ത്ത് ഇന്‍സ്പെക്ടറെ മരിച്ച നിലയില്‍ കണ്ടെത്തി Media Oneപുന്നയൂര്‍ കുടുംബരോഗ്യ കേന്ദ്രത്തിലെ ജൂനിയര്‍ ഹെല്‍ത്ത് ഇന്‍സ്‌പെക്ടറെ ക്വാട്ടേഴ്സിൽ മരിച്ച നിലയില്‍ കണ്ടെത്തി Asianet News Malayalamകുടുംബാരോഗ്യ കേന്ദ്രത്തിലെ ജൂനിയര്‍ ഹെല്‍ത്ത് ഇന്‍സ്പെക്ടറെ മരിച്ച നിലയില്‍ കണ്ടെത്തി Kerala Vision Newsജൂനിയർ ഹെൽത്ത് ഇൻസ്പെക്ടറെ ജോലിസ്ഥലത്ത് മരിച്ച നിലയിൽ കണ്ടെത്തി Samakalika Malayalamചാവക്കാട് ജൂനിയർ ഹെൽത്ത് ഇൻസ്‌പെക്ടറെ മരിച്ച നിലയിൽ കണ്ടത്തി Kairali News O

items.story: Research by INRAE and AgroParisTech suggests that global warming could have an overall positive effect on sorghum yields in Europe. Sorghum is a promising alternative to maize in livestock feed. Additionally, the crop requires less water and can tolerate higher temperatures. The researchers carried out simulations that used past climate data and future climate scenarios with the broader goal of developing new strategies for European agriculture. Their results were published in Earth's Future.

items.headline: Physicists just saw quarks make waves in the Big Bang’s primordial soup
items.teaser: Physicists at CERN’s Large Hadron Collider have captured the clearest evidence yet that quark-gluon plasma, the scorching-hot matter that…
items.story: Physicists at CERN’s Large Hadron Collider have captured the clearest evidence yet that quark-gluon plasma, the scorching-hot matter that filled the newborn universe, behaves like a true liquid. By tracking individual quarks as they blasted through the plasma, researchers saw them leave behind ripples, splashes, and swirling wakes much like a duck moving through water. The finding suggests this primordial “soup” is so dense that it can slow speeding quarks and respond collectively as a fluid.
